caption:
San Antonio, through a car window.

A phone on the glass films a street in one of the city's 32 study areas. Software picks out the dogs.

Southwest Research Institute and Animal Care Services are repeating the city's hand count from 2019. Automated and human review then checks each clip.

Owned or stray is read from appearance. "Strays appear to be malnourished and skittish," the release says. Healthier and more approachable dogs count as roaming.

Pull back from that street and a city is letting software take the first look. ACS Director Jon Gary calls it another tool to see where loose dogs turn up. Both partners say it is a sample, not a count of every dog.

The deck follows one clip from lens to report.

When the final report reaches Animal Care Services after December, will it say how often reviewers disagreed with the software?
